source.stem:
The structures of four molecules are shown.

Which molecules belong to the same homologous series?

intelligence.enrichment: Metals are generally lustrous, hard, malleable, ductile, sonorous, and good conductors of heat and electricity; most non-metals lack these properties. Sodium and potassium are soft metals, and mercury is a liquid metal at room temperature. Observed material properties support classification as metal or non-metal, with exceptions checked before making the final classification. The learner correctly applies this rule: Metals are generally lustrous, hard, malleable, ductile, sonorous, and good conductors of heat and electricity; most non-metals lack these properties. Sodium and potassium are soft metals, and mercury is a liquid metal at room temperature. Metals are always hard, shiny solids, so anything soft or liquid is a non-metal.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 7 Science question. Chapter: The world of metals and non-metals. The student must decide: When a material is observed, decide whether its lustre, hardness, malleability, ductility, sonority, and conductivity point to a metal or to a non-metal, while allowing named exceptions. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Retarget the source onto this Science decision. Keep the source item type. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE.
